title: Site-perfect models in a prescribed Tor interval
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and module-sheaf category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localization and restriction to $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ be locally perfect: for every $U\in\mathcal C$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ on which $E|_{U_i}$ is isomorphic to a bounded cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module sheaves, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers, and suppose the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] satisfy $H^r(E\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}F)=0$ for every $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $F$ in degree zero and every $r\notin[a,b]$. Then for every $U$ there is a covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ and bounded cochain complexes $P_j$ of $\mathcal O_{V_j}$-modules, with each $P_j^r$ a direct summand of a finite free module sheaf, such that $P_j^r=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ and $P_j\cong E|_{V_j}$ in $D(\mathcal O_{V_j})$.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), proof: the final displayed strictly perfect complex in degrees a through b; apply to a locally perfect E. Restriction of the Tor interval: Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback). Upper-end shortening by local split surjections is explained also in the preceding pseudo-coherence section.

proof.text: Fix $U\in\mathcal C$. Choose a covering and bounded finite-projective models $P$ of $E$ there, with explicit degreewise splittings as retracts of finite free sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Work on each of these slice sites. By [lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction], the restriction of $E$ has the same Tor interval $[a,b]$, testing against every module sheaf on this slice, not just restrictions of global test sheaves. Thus $H^r(P\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ on this slice.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), first local replacement, and Tag 08H5 (lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback).

proof.text: Every term of $P$ is flat in the sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]: by the additive tensor structure and its unit in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], tensoring with a retract of $\mathcal O^{\oplus s}$ is a retract of the exact functor $F\mapsto F^{\oplus s}$, so preserves exact sequences. Hence [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $P$ K-flat. For any degree-zero module $F$, the ordinary complex $P\otimes F$ computes $P\otimes^{\mathbf L}F$: take a K-flat flat-term resolution $T\to F[0]$ supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; its cone is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. The natural complex isomorphism of [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso], applied with $\mathcal A^\bullet=P$ and $K_1\to K_2$ equal to $T\to F[0]$, identifies the cone of $P\otimes T\to P\otimes F[0]$ with $P\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(T\to F[0])$. Thus K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes $P\otimes T\to P\otimes F[0]$ a quasi-isomorphism, again by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Since both $P$ and $T$ are K-flat with flat terms, [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies $P\otimes T$ with the derived tensor of their represented objects. Termwise tensor symmetry identifies $F\otimes P$ with $P\otimes F[0]$. Taking $F=\mathcal O$ gives $H^r(P)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. This computation applies to every bounded finite-projective model constructed below.

Let $n>b$ be a degree above which the current model is zero. Then $H^n(P)=0$ makes $d:P^{n-1}\to P^n$ an epimorphism. Choose a retraction $P^n\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal O^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{p}P^n$. Forgetting modules preserves epimorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], each of the finitely many sections $p(e_j)$ lifts along $d$ after a cover; successively refine to lift them all on one cover. These lifts give $h:\mathcal O^{\oplus s}\to P^{n-1}$ with $dh=p$, hence $s_0=hi:P^n\to P^{n-1}$ satisfies $ds_0=\operatorname{id}$. This argument uses only local section lifts, not surjectivity on sections over the original object.

source.place: Tag 08FN (lemma-local-lift-map), written out; Tag 08FX (lemma-finite-cohomology), upper shortening in the proof of (1).

proof.text: On each member of this cover put $K=\ker d$. The maps $x\mapsto(x-s_0d(x),d(x))$ and $(k,y)\mapsto k+s_0(y)$ identify $P^{n-1}$ with $K\oplus P^n$. Consequently $K$ is a retract of $P^{n-1}$ and hence of a finite free sheaf. Since $dd^{n-2}=0$, the incoming differential lands in $K$. The complex is therefore the direct sum of the shortened complex (replace $P^{n-1}$ by $K$ and $P^n$ by zero) and the two-term identity complex $P^n\xrightarrow{1}P^n$ in degrees $n-1,n$. The latter has contracting homotopy the identity backwards, so removing it gives a quasi-isomorphism and preserves the represented derived object.

source.place: Tag 08FX (lemma-finite-cohomology), proof of (1), explicit splitting and induction step.

proof.text: Choose an initial integer upper bound $t\ge b$ for $P$. Descending induction from $n=t$ through $n=b+1$ using Steps 3 and 4 produces, after a finite succession of covers on this original perfect chart, a bounded finite-projective complex $Q$ zero in degrees $>b$. The base case $t=b$ needs no change; if a top term is zero the splitting is the zero map. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], hence preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and restricts the displayed retractions sectionwise. At every refinement [lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction] preserves the Tor interval of the represented object. Iterated slices are slices of the original site by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; transitivity of covers composes these finite refinements. Thus $Q$ still represents the appropriate restriction of $E$ and has Tor interval $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 08FX (lemma-finite-cohomology), upper shortening; Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), the upper bound implicit in its final displayed complex.

proof.text: Set $N=\operatorname{coker}(d_Q^{a-1}:Q^{a-1}\to Q^a)$. By Step 2 applied to $Q$, for every module sheaf $F$ the ordinary complex $F\otimes Q$ has zero cohomology in degree $a-1$. The terms of $Q$ are flat. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion], applied on the current small slice site with $n=a$, proves that $N$ is flat. This uses the site's general opcycle criterion; no assumption of enough points or of constant coefficients is made.

source.place: Tag 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat) and Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), flatness of the lower-end cokernel.

proof.text:
The sheaf $N$ has a finite presentation. To see it directly, write retractions $Q^a\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal O^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{p}Q^a$ and $Q^{a-1}\xrightarrow{j}\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{q}Q^{a-1}$ with $pi=1$ and $qj=1$, and put $e=ip$. Then
$$\mathcal O^{\oplus s}\oplus\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{(1-e,\ i d_Q^{a-1}q)}\mathcal O^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{\overline p}N\to0$$
is exact: $\ker p=\operatorname{im}(1-e)$ and the image of $id_Q^{a-1}q$ is $i(\operatorname{im}d_Q^{a-1})$, so the cokernel is precisely $Q^a/\operatorname{im}d_Q^{a-1}$. These identities hold as sheaf images and cokernels, with no exactness of global sections asserted. Thus $N$ satisfies the explicit finite-presentation hypothesis of Step 8.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), finite presentation before the invocation of Modules on Sites Tag 08FD; explicit presentation from the degreewise retractions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-site-flat-fp-finite-retract] to $N$ on this slice, using Steps 6 and 7. On its resulting cover form $R$ with $R^a=N$, $R^r=Q^r$ for $a<r\le b$, and zero terms otherwise; its first differential is induced by $d_Q^a$, which annihilates $\operatorname{im}d_Q^{a-1}$. Restrict this construction to each covering member. Exact restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] preserves its quotient and cohomology. The quotient chain map $Q\to R$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology: in degree $a$ its kernel calculation is $\ker(d_Q^a)/\operatorname{im}(d_Q^{a-1})$, in degree $a+1$ the incoming image is unchanged because $Q^a\to N$ is an epimorphism and $d_Q^a$ factors through it, in degrees $>a+1$ the adjacent terms and differentials are identical, and below $a$ both cohomologies vanish by the given Tor interval and Step 2. Hence $R$ represents the restriction of $E$. Its degree $a$ term is a finite free retract by the new tool and its other terms retain their retractions. It is zero outside $[a,b]$. Finally compose all covers with the original perfect cover using [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and the covering transitivity axiom to get the asserted $\{V_j\to U\}$.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), final displayed complex, with Tag 08FD (sites-modules-lemma-flat-locally-finite-presentation).

proof_origin.place: Tags 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat), 08FX (lemma-finite-cohomology), and 08FN (lemma-local-lift-map); the local perfect model supplies the pseudo-coherent approximation directly. Generic complex isomorphism for total tensor and a mapping cone; supplies the signed comparison needed in Step 2.
